segments.arabic:
١١٤٨٥- عفراء بنت عبيد
بن ثعلبة بن سواد بن غنم «٣»، ويقال ثعلبة بن عبيد بن ثعلبة بن غنم بن مالك بن النجار.
ذكرها ابن حبيب في المبايعات، وهي والدة معاذ، ومعوذ، وعوف بني الحارث، يقال لكل منهم ابن عفراء.
وقال ابن سعد: أمها الرعاة بنت عدي بن معاذ، تزوّجها الحارث بن رفاعة بن الحارث بن سواد، فولدت له.
قال ابن الكلبيّ: قتل معاذ ومعوذ، فجاءت أمّهما إلى النبيّ ﵌ فقالت: يا رسول اللَّه، هذا سرّ بني عوف بن الحارث. فقال: «لا» .
قال ابن الأثير: لم يوافق ابن الكلبي على قوله: إن معاذا قتل ببدر.
قلت: وعفراء هذه لها خصيصة لا توجد لغيرها، وهي أنها تزوّجت بعد الحارث البكير بن يا ليل الليثي، فولدت له أربعة: إياسا، وعاقلا، وخالدا، وعامرا، وكلّهم شهدوا بدرا، وكذلك إخوتهم لأمهم بنو الحارث، فانتظم من هذا أنها امرأة صحابية لها سبعة أولاد شهدوا كلهم بدرا مع النبي ﵌.
(١) في أ: ابن عزيزة.
(٢) أسد الغابة ت (٧١١٠) .
(٣) أسد الغابة ت (٧١١٢) .
segments.english:
11485—Afra bint Ubayd

ibn Thalaba ibn Sawad ibn Ghanm;(3) it is also said: Thalaba ibn Ubayd ibn Thalaba ibn Ghanm ibn Malik ibn al-Najjar.

Ibn Habib mentioned her among the women who pledged allegiance. She was the mother of Muadh, Muawwidh, and Awf, the sons of al-Harith; each of them was called Ibn Afra.

Ibn Sad said: Her mother was al-Ru'at bint Adi ibn Muadh. Al-Harith ibn Rifaa ibn al-Harith ibn Sawad married her, and she bore him children.

Ibn al-Kalbi said: Muadh and Muawwidh were killed, whereupon their mother came to the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—and said, “O Messenger of Allah, this is the choicest of my sons: Awf ibn al-Harith.” He said, “No.”

Ibn al-Athir said: Ibn al-Kalbi was not corroborated in his statement that Muadh was killed at Badr.

I say: This Afra possessed a distinction found in no other woman: after al-Harith, she married al-Bukayr ibn Yalil al-Laythi and bore him four sons—Iyas, Aqil, Khalid, and Amir—all of whom witnessed Badr. Their maternal brothers, the sons of al-Harith, did so as well. It thus follows that she was a woman Companion who had seven sons, all of whom witnessed Badr with the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

(1) In A: “ibn Aziza.”

(2) Usd al-Ghaba, entry (7110).

(3) Usd al-Ghaba, entry (7112).

names.english: al-Harith ibn Rifaa ibn al-Harith ibn Sawad

unresolved.explanation: The consonantal form is clear, but neither the canonical text nor the Urdu witness supplies vowels sufficient to establish its precise pronunciation. The final text provisionally uses al-Ru'at.

unresolved.arabic_span: هذا سرّ بني عوف بن الحارث
unresolved.explanation: The canonical text has سرّ (“choicest”), although the reply “No” is contextually difficult and Usd al-Ghaba instead has شر (“worst”). Because the canonical al-Isabah is authoritative, the final text preserves “choicest” and does not import the collateral reading.
